clues.title: Plate: Bangladeshi licence plates are either white
text: Bangladeshi licence plates are either **white**, **black** or **turquoise**.
NOTE: The turquoise plate can only be found in Bangladesh.

clues.title: Language: The Bengali script features a continuous horizontal line at…
text: The Bengali script features a continuous **horizontal line** at the top of each word. It has a similar look to [Devanagari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devanagari) (Hindi and Nepali), however it can usually be recognised by the many letters featuring triangular shapes.
NOTE: Bengali is an official language in Bangladesh and parts of eastern India.

clues.title: Google car: In Generation 3 coverage
text: In Generation 3 coverage, these three cars can be seen in Bangladesh: the **red mirror with bars**, **classic white** and **striped white** car.
NOTE: The classic white car is the only car that is not unique to Bangladesh. Make sure to not mix up the striped white with the Cambodian car, since they look similar.

clues.title: Google car: In Generation 4 coverage
text: In Generation 4 coverage, two Street View cars can be seen in Bangladesh: a black car and a white car.

clues.title: Coverage: Bangladesh, as well as a variety of other countries, has…
text: Bangladesh, as well as a variety of other countries, has received some poor quality coverage, also known as “Shitcam”. The Shitcam car colours are [black](https://www.google.com/maps/@23.6593897,90.4855596,3a,63.7y,83.56h,57.38t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s1pCZPeT5RHbSzl-lSifVeQ!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) and [white](https://www.google.com/maps/@23.8892702,90.3897794,3a,63.4y,163.13h,54.23t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s-PLvXV5yN94xzegYGmO5TQ!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu).

NOTE: Sometimes the car colour can be fully obstructed by a [big circular blur](https://www.google.com/maps/@23.6938128,90.5200604,3a,90y,72.06h,50.06t,0.36r/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1se3JEcXu6CviGqaDTACJrhw!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu).

clues.title: Rickshaws are frequently found all around Bangladesh
text: **Rickshaws** are frequently found all around Bangladesh, especially the green auto rickshaws.
NOTE: They are found in other Asian countries as well.

clues.title: Direction sign: Signposts in Bangladesh often have black-and-white stripes
text: Signposts in Bangladesh often have **black-and-white stripes**.
NOTE: Within Asia, these posts are also found in Sri Lanka, Bhutan, India, Nepal and Malaysia. Make sure to check other clues before guessing.

clues.title: Bodies of water and agricultural fields can be often seen…
text: **Bodies of water** and **agricultural fields** can be often seen beside the streets of Bangladesh.

clues.title: Vegetation: Streets in Bangladesh are often lined by trees
text: Streets in Bangladesh are often lined by trees, which sometimes have **white paint** on the bottom of their trunks.

clues.title: Bollard: Bangladesh uses red-and-white concrete bollards throughout…
text: Bangladesh uses **red-and-white** concrete bollards throughout the whole country.
NOTE: They can also be found in a square form instead of a circular form.

clues.title: Architecture: Tin roofs are commonly found in Bangladesh
text: **Tin roofs** are commonly found in Bangladesh.
NOTE: Due to the humid climate, many countries in South and Southeast Asia use tin roofs.

clues.title: Google car: The Generation 4 coverage in Bangladesh will often have a…
text: The Generation 4 coverage in Bangladesh will often have a **smoky** feel to it.

clues.title: Architecture: Bangladesh has several distinct roof styles that create an…
text: Bangladesh has several distinct roof styles that create an **east/west** divide in the country.

The west, particularly the divisions of Rajshahi, Khulna and Dhaka, is dominated by [hip roofs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_roof) made of sheet metal. The states of Rangpur and Chittagong tend to have mixed roofs.

clues.title: Architecture: In the east, you will commonly see sheet metal roofs with a…
text: In the east, you will commonly see sheet metal roofs with a** triangular "window"** just below the ridge of the roof. The state of Sylhet will exclusively have this style, which can also be seen in Chittagong, Mymensingh, eastern Rangpur and northern Dhaka.

clues.title: Architecture: Tiled roofs are uncommon in Bangladesh
text: **Tiled roofs** are uncommon in Bangladesh, but the ones you do see are of West Bengal origin, and are thus only found on the Indian border in the state of Khulna.

clues.title: Google car: Rice is the main agricultural crop in Bangladesh and is…
text: Rice is the main agricultural crop in Bangladesh and is planted twice a year. The different rice seasons can be told apart by the height and colour of the rice and are very useful for regionguessing.

**Short green rice** that is barely sticking out of the water is known as **early growth rice**. Early growth rice can be seen in the states of** **Khulna, Mymensingh and south of Padma River in Dhaka.
NOTE: Beware that this, and the following tips, are only accurate in Generation 4 coverage.

clues.title: Slightly taller rice, in the middle of growing, which still…
text: Slightly taller rice, in the **middle of growing**, which still remains **green**, can be seen in the states of Rangpur, Barishal and Chittagong.

clues.title: Fully-grown rice is characterised by being noticeably taller
text: **Fully-grown rice** is characterised by being noticeably taller, as well as having a** yellow** or **orange colour** and **fluffier tips** - the fluffiness signifies that the rice is ripe. Fully-grown rice is mostly seen in the state of Rajshahi, but it is also present in Rangpur and Chittagong.

clues.title: Harvested rice can be identified by its beige or brown…
text: **Harvested rice** can be identified by its **beige or brown colour** and **shorter, cut down appearance**. It can be seen alongside fully-grown, unharvested rice as well as freshly planted early growth rice in adjacent fields. This is most commonly seen in the states of Sylhet and southern Khulna.

clues.title: Rice fields require some rest time
text: Rice fields require some **rest time**, so it's natural to come across some off-season **barren, empty fields** without rice altogether. Off-season fields are mostly seen in the state of Dhaka, north of Padma River.

clues.title: Vast rice fields with almost nothing else in view can be…
text: Vast rice fields with almost nothing else in view can be seen in the border area between the states of Dhaka, Mymensingh and Sylhet.

clues.title: Landscape: While most of Bangladesh is almost completely flat
text: While most of Bangladesh is almost completely flat, in the eastern parts of Chittagong you may find fairly tall, forested and uncultivated **hills**.

clues.title: A sizable east-west ridge can be seen on the Indian border…
text: A sizable east-west ridge can be seen on the Indian border from the northern parts of Sylhet and eastern Mymensingh. It is often obscured or diminished by heavy haze.

clues.title: Corn tends to be planted in the west of Bangladesh
text: **Corn** tends to be planted in the west of Bangladesh - large and medium-sized fields can be found in Rajshahi, Rangpur, western Mymensingh and northern Khulna.
Smaller patches of corn can be found in the [south of Barishal](https://maps.app.goo.gl/QG6LM1Zzrf3vgCfo6), usually adjacent to other crops.

clues.title: Coverage: Jute is a tall-growing green crop which gets dried and used…
text: [Jute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jute) is a tall-growing green crop which gets dried and used in the making of rugs, bags and other goods. Because of when the coverage was taken, jute can almost exclusively be found on Street View in Rangpur. In its dried state it can be found hanging off fences and drying on the roads anywhere in the country.

clues.title: Canola is a low-growing crop with yellow flowers that is…
text: **Canola** is a** **low-growing crop with **yellow flowers** that is used to make cooking oil. It is usually planted during the off-season for rice, making it extremely common north of Padma river in the state of Dhaka.

clues.title: Tea production in Bangladesh is concentrated in the…
text: **Tea production** in Bangladesh is concentrated in the highlands of southern Sylhet and, rarely, Chittagong.

clues.title: Vegetation: Standalone fruit trees in Bangladesh are most commonly seen…
text: Standalone **fruit trees** in Bangladesh are most commonly seen in the states of Rajshahi and Rangpur.** Fruit orchards** with systematically planted trees, however, are concentrated near the Indian border in both states.

clues.title: Sunflower fields are found in the south of Barishal state
text: **Sunflower fields** are found in the south of Barishal state.

clues.title: Fields of watermelons can also be found in the south of…
text: Fields of **watermelons **can also be found in the south of Barishal.

clues.title: Vegetation: Eucalyptus trees are tall trees with lush crowns and…
text: **Eucalyptus trees** are** **tall trees with lush crowns and **ivory-coloured trunks**. In Bangladesh they are more common in the north, with** **Rangpur, Rajshahi and Mymensingh being the most likely states.

clues.title: Vegetation: Blossoming trees are tied to coverage and seasonal metas in…
text: **Blossoming trees** are tied to coverage and seasonal metas in Bangladesh, and are only found in the states where coverage was taken during spring time - Khulna, Mymensingh and southern Dhaka.
NOTE: Beware that this is only accurate in Generation 4 coverage.

clues.title: Vegetation: Beach Sheoaks (Casuarina equisetifolia) are thin evergreen…
text: **Beach Sheoaks **([Casuarina equisetifolia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casuarina_equisetifolia)) are thin evergreen trees** **with **thin, long, drooping branchlets. **Like the name suggests, they are mostly observed in coastal regions - along the coast of the Teknaf Peninsula and around Noakhali city in Chittagong.

clues.title: Coverage: For legal reasons, Google has added small labels noting…
text: For legal reasons, Google has added small labels noting their copyright on all Street View coverage. These labels contain a year, typically the year when the coverage was released, which can be used to regionguess Bangladesh. Generation 4 coverage with **2022** written on the copyright labels can be found in Mymensingh, Dhaka and less commonly Chittagong.
NOTE: Beware that the copyright labels will rarely get updated to a later year, without any other changes to the coverage.

clues.title: Google car: Similarly, Generation 4 coverage with 2023 written on the…
text: Similarly, Generation 4 coverage with **2023** written on the copyright labels can be found in Rangpur, Rajshahi, Khulna, Barishal, Sylhet and less commonly Chittagong.
NOTE: 2024 and 2025 now make up around half of all copyright dates. These can be found all over the country.

clues.title: Coverage: Shitcam coverage is only found in and around Dhaka
text: **Shitcam coverage** is only found in and around Dhaka.

clues.title: Google car: Generation 3 coverage with the white Street View car can be…
text: **Generation 3** coverage with the **white** Street View car can be found in Dhaka, Chattogram as well as on the highway connecting them.

clues.title: Google car: Generation 3 coverage with the striped Street View car can…
text: **Generation 3** coverage with the **striped **Street View car can be found mostly on yellow roads west of Dhaka.

clues.title: Google car: In the city of Sylhet there will often be a guard at the…
text: In the city of Sylhet there will often be a **guard** at the side of the car visible, usually holding a hayfork. Note that this only applies to Generation 3 coverage.

clues.title: Coverage: In the city of Barishal there can also be a guard at the…
text: In the city of Barishal there can also be a **guard** at the side of the car visible, not to be confused with the Sylhet guard.
NOTE: The [same man](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ZRAD485rKUBixpPU8) can rarely be found elsewhere on trekker coverage.

clues.title: Coverage: This interesting trekker with a black cover can be found in…
text: This interesting trekker with a black cover can be found in the city of **Khulna**.

clues.title: Coverage: The trekker with red colour in the mirrors is unique to the…
text: The trekker with **red colour** in the mirrors is unique to the island of Nijhum Dwip.

clues.title: Coverage: A scooter trekker, where mostly the left mirror and some…
text: A scooter trekker, where mostly the **left mirror** and some **hair** is visible, can be found on Hatiya Island.

clues.title: Coverage: A trekker escorted by a security guard is found on Saint…
text: A trekker escorted by a **security guard** is found on Saint Martin's Island.

clues.title: Plate: Bangladesh
text: Bangladeshi licence plates are either white, black or turquoise.
NOTE: The turquoise plate can only be found in Bangladesh.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Angular Fender Bars Roofed Cycle Rickshaws
text: Roofed cycle rickshaws with **angular fenders** with **painted metal bars on top** can be found in **Mymensingh Division**. The roof will often be folded back.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Barishal Roofed Cycle Rickshaws
text: Roofed cycle rickshaws with these **distinctive rear axle ornaments** are only found in **Barishal Division**. There are two common variants: a simpler design with an upside-down heart shape in the centre and a more ornate one with a circular design in the centre.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Chariotlike Cycle Rickshaws
text: **Chariot-like cycle and auto rickshaws** with this distinctive style of large passenger seat are only found **between Gazipur and Mawna in Dhaka Division.**

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Chittagong Roofed Cycle Rickshaws
text: Roofed cycle rickshaws with **multiple lines above the rear axle** can be found in some areas of **southern Chittagong Division** and are particularly common in the city of **Chittagong**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Cross Bench Cycle Rickshaws
text: Cycle rickshaws with a **cross bench** (oriented perpendicular to the driving direction) and often painted in a **striped blue-red-yellow pattern** can be found **between Tangail and Dhaka.**

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Double Rounded Cross Pattern Cycle Rickshaws
text: Flatbed cycle rickshaws with this pattern of quarter circles and semicircles, forming a **‘double rounded cross’ pattern**, can be seen in **eastern Dhaka Division** and across the border in **Khulna Division**, near **Magura**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Jeeps
text: These **jeep-style utility vehicles** appear predominantly in **Chittagong division**, especially in the **Chittagong Hill Tracts**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Long Bench Back Bars Cycle Rickshaws
text: Cycle rickshaws with **long benches** (oriented parallel to the driving direction) and **decorative metal bars at the back** can be found **north-west of Naogaon**. These rickshaws will not have a cross bench behind the driver's seat.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Long Bench Cycle Rickshaws
text: Cycle rickshaws with **long benches** (oriented parallel to the driving direction) and **without rear decorations or a cross bench** can be commonly seen in **northern Rajshahi Division** and **south-eastern Rangpur Division**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Long Plank Cycle Rickshaws
text: Flatbed cycle rickshaws with **long planks, oriented parallel to the driving direction**, can rarely be found all around the country, however they are by far most common in **north-western Rangpur Division** and rarely in **north-western Mymensingh Division**, along the border with India.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Metal Carts and Cycle Rickshaws
text: Pulled carts and cycle rickshaws with **metal cage-like frames** are commonly used in **Sylhet Division** and rarely in **Chittagong Division**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Patgram Cycle Rickshaws
text: Similar cycle rickshaws with **two long benches and a cross bench in a ‘U’ formation** but with **wooden vertical extensions** visible on both sides of rear wheels, are only found **around the town of Patgram in northern Rangpur Division**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Rectangular Frame Cycle Rickshaws
text: Additionally, flatbed cycle rickshaws with a **rectangular metal frame** under the driver’s seat, are commonly found in **far north-west Rangpur Division**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: St
text: These cycle rickshaws with **long benches** and **ridged roofs** are only used on **St. Martin’s Island**, in the far south of Bangladesh.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Rounded Cross Pattern Cycle Rickshaws
text: Flatbed cycle rickshaws with this pattern of corner quarter circles, forming a **‘rounded cross’ pattern** can often be seen in **northern Khulna Division, east of Pabna in Rajshahi Division** and in **central Rajshahi Division**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Tunnel-like Roofed Cycle Rickshaws
text: Cycle rickshaws with **arched tunnel-like roofs** extending over the driver’s seat are only used in two separate areas near the border with India: **south of Satkhira** and **south of Meherpur**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: U Bench Cycle Rickshaws
text: Cycle rickshaws with **two long benches and a cross bench in a ‘U’ formation** are commonly found in **eastern Rajshahi Division** and part of **southern Rangpur Division**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Wooden Fender Cycle Rickshaws
text: Flatbed cycle rickshaws with **horizontal wooden extensions** above the rear wheels are most commonly found **north-east of Tangail** and in part of **southern Mymensingh Division**, but can also be seen in **Magura**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Bent Bar Auto Rickshaws
text: A high proportion of auto rickshaws in **Mymensingh Division** have a **metal bar over the top of the front roof area** with a **slight but noticeable upward bend**. They may or may not have small metal ball shapes on them, either on each side or along the bar. You see similar metal bars in other regions occasionally, but they are normally unbent.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Chittagong Auto Rickshaws
text: Auto rickshaws in **Chittagong** often feature a variety of decorations and characteristics which are unlikely to appear in other parts of Bangladesh. These include:
**Long lines of Arabic calligraphy** written **above the windshield** *(not just the single word Allah, الله, which is commonplace) *
**Semicircular grill ornaments** (as opposed to pointed or ‘onion-dome’-shaped)

Grill ornaments flanked by **a pair of upward-pointing ‘bulbous cage’ metal ornaments** Most auto rickshaws in Chittagong do not have all of these features, but seeing one or more of them on an auto rickshaw is a good clue for this division.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Colored Front Auto Rickshaws
text: Green auto rickshaws in this part of **western Chittagong Division** will usually have **all or half of the front painted in a different bright solid colour**, such as yellow, red or blue. When half is painted it may be the upper or lower half. While it is possible to rarely find such auto rickshaws elsewhere, they will only constitute a majority in this area.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Curly Dome Auto Rickshaw Ornaments
text: This distinctive grill ornament featuring **two curled scroll shapes** appears **in Chittagong Division** to the north of Chittagong . It remains a fairly-reliable indicator for this region even when positioned elsewhere on the rickshaw , such as on the side above the back wheels.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: South Barishal Auto Rickshaws
text: This **grill ornament** featuring a **semicircle over an onion-dome shape** appears on the front of electric auto rickshaws to the **south of the city of Barishal**, roughly between the Payra and Tetulia rivers.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: VIP Auto Rickshaw Covers
text: This **distinctive style of roof covering** is seen on some electric auto rickshaws in **western Rajshahi Division** and **southern Rangpur Division**. The covering usually features **the text ‘VIP’** although custom variants with other initials also exist. The colour scheme can vary but will be two-tone or three-tone.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Welcome Auto Rickshaws
text: **South and east of the city of Sylhet**, you can somewhat commonly see auto rickshaws with **the text ‘Well Come’ or ‘Welcome’** on the side roof area, above or behind the door.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
